static_traits.name: Zhang Jingwen
static_traits.family_status: Lives with parents; one sister and a niece
static_traits.social_status: Mainly relies on family support, especially her older sister; due to the pressure of studies and caring for her parents, her relationship with her family was tense for a while recently
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; never received psychotherapy before; no similar academic fears in the past
static_traits.language_features: High cooperativeness, clear expression, can describe anxiety and automatic thoughts; tendencies toward catastrophizing, negating the positive, and predicting failure; overall positive attitude

basic_info.main_problem: I worry I will be unable to pass my degree's final exams, though I am close to completing the degree.
basic_info.core_demands: Fear of exam failure leads to strong distress and affects study focus, thus hoping to obtain professional support to relieve academic fear and improve focus and exam-preparation efficiency.
growth_experiences: Long living with parents while studying for the degree and bearing caregiving duties, needing to switch between family caregiving and studies. With final exams approaching, conflicts over time and energy allocation intensify, bringing marked pressure; family relationships grow tense too.

Previously good overall performance in coursework exams and learning tasks: regular attendance, on-time homework, and decent scores in past tests, but facing the final key exam, unprecedented strong feelings of academic inadequacy and failure fear began to appear.

core_beliefs: I am not competent enough / insufficient ability, failing at key moments
If I fail this exam, all prior efforts will not count and will disappoint others

special_situations.event: Lying in bed at night thinking about the upcoming final exam
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I fail this key exam, all my efforts will be reduced to zero
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Seeking reassurance from family, worrying repeatedly in her mind to 'prepare in advance'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will surely fail; all my efforts may be in vain.

special_situations.event: When starting revision, focusing attention on content she 'does not understand'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If there are still many knowledge points I do not know, it means I have not prepared well and will surely fail
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubling learning, constantly expanding the learning list to 'make up inadequacy'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I know too little, surely I will not pass like this.

special_situations.event: Recalling past good test scores, but seeing this one as 'different and more important'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Past scores do not represent ability; only passing this time proves I have value
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating past successes, continuously raising standards to force herself to learn
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Doing well before means nothing for this time; this time is harder, more critical, I will still fail.

special_situations.event: Switches back and forth between caring for parents and preparing for exams, with time frequently interrupted
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot handle both caregiving and learning well, I will fail and disappoint my family
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to juggle everything, compressing rest time to keep both learning and caregiving from 'dropping off'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I cannot manage it all, I will fail in the end, and disappoint everyone.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to prove herself competent and be recognized by important others, not disappointing family
core_conflict.fear: Fears that failure will lead to shame and evaluation, and letting down the family's expectations
defense_goal: Prevents feelings of failure through excessive worry and high standards
Temporarily lowering anxiety by seeking reassurance
Maintaining a sense of control over uncertainty through constantly redoubled effort

object_relations.self_representation: A 'duty-bearer' who must be competent as both student and caregiver, possibly doing not well enough at any time
object_relations.object_representation: The other party (family/significant others) is experienced as an evaluator with expectations who may be disappointed

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor invites him to review past successes or look at real evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to use 'this time is different and more important' as a reason, believing past successes have no reference value
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gentle tone, first empathizing with her pressure, then guiding her with concretizing questions to list both supporting and refuting evidence, gradually testing the basis of 'this time is different'.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about 'fearing disappointing everyone' and internalizing others' expectations as pressure
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Attributes others' high expectations and disappointment to the other party (assuming others will judge oneself harshly)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using clarification and boundary-setting questions, distinguishing fact from speculation, encouraging her to express needs and boundaries in the first person, reducing speculation about others' thoughts.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to consider both passing and not-yet-passing outcomes and prepare for each
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Trying to gain a sense of control through planning and preparation amid anxiety
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Reinforcing her effective preparation behaviors, using a supportive tone, helping normalize goal breakdown and progress review, consolidating reality-testing.

manifestations: Feels torn between caring for parents and self-development (completing the degree), experiencing the tension between choice and responsibility
Worries that failure will disappoint others' expectations; personal choices seem limited by family responsibility
outcomes: Sleep and diet rhythms disrupted,Decreased concentration

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Repeatedly self-evaluates and worries about 'disappointing everyone', worsening inner pressure
In exam preparation, persistent self-blame, finding it hard to allow himself to acknowledge progress made

contact_model.definition: The individual ignores or avoids a stimulus from the internal or external environment, deliberately avoiding direct contact.
manifestations: When invited to review past successes, deflecting attention to 'this time is different, harder', avoiding positive evidence
Continuously deflecting attention to 'not understood' parts during revision, ignoring mastered content

positive_force: Good past test performance, with experience of learning investment and task completion
Continuous regular study (attendance, notes, homework completed)
Family support available, especially the elder sister's emotional support
Positive attitude, proactively seeks help and is willing to try reality testing and goal breakdown
negative_force: Cognitive habits of catastrophizing, predicting the future, and negating the positive reinforcing anxiety
The role conflict between caring for parents and exam preparation disperses time and energy
Anxiety running high in learning and bedtime situations, affecting focus, sleep, and diet
Relying on others' reassurance bringing short-term relief, maintaining the anxiety cycle long-term

target_behavior.behavior: Catastrophic worries and anticipated failure about final exams, with significant anxiety
antecedent: When starting to study or review
Lying in bed at night thinking about the upcoming exam
Returning to the study situation after being interrupted by family care matters
target_behavior.core_reason: Under the dual pressure of care responsibilities and academic goals, forms a catastrophic cognition of failure and infers negative outcomes from it
target_behavior.function: Escaping uncertainty, seeking control over outcomes to briefly lower anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased attention, impaired study efficiency, sleep and diet rhythm disturbance, further weakening exam-prep state

target_behavior.behavior: Repeatedly seeking reassurance from family (such as asking whether one will pass, whether one is fully prepared)
antecedent: When learning is blocked or thinking of 'still unknown' content
Exam approaching, periods of rising anxiety
target_behavior.core_reason: Lacking confidence in her own ability, tending to rely on external validation to ease uncertainty
target_behavior.function: Gaining emotional soothing and immediate anxiety relief
target_behavior.consequence: Short-term anxiety drops, but long-term reinforcement of the dependence-and-worry cycle, maintaining distrust of her own ability
